thread.title: Apple tests security feature that could foil law enforcement

author: Channel365
title: Apple tests security feature that could foil law enforcement
text:
Feature would plug security loophole that allowed gain access to from USB port
Bloomberg News The Lighting connector port on an iPhone 7. Apple Inc. stated it is working on a new security feature that could make it harder for investigators to recover data from iPhones, the current twist in its long-running standoff with law-enforcement companies over user privacy.The new software feature, called USB Restricted Mode, is being beta-tested by Apple. It avoids other devices– individual computers, for example– from accessing information on the iPhone via its Lightning port an hour after a phone is last unlocked.Apple
AAPL, +0.65%, in its first public talk about the function, said Wednesday that it was created to improve the security of Apple’s devices versus all type of prospective trespassers.”We have the best respect for law enforcement, and we do not create our security enhancements to frustrate their efforts to do their jobs,”the business stated in a statement.The change might plug a security loophole used by companies that make forensics tools, who have just recently had more success in getting access to Apple’s gadgets.
One company, Atlanta’s GrayShift LLC, sells a$15,000 USB-connected gadget that it claims can open the latest iPhones. Another business, Cellebrite Mobile Synchronization Ltd., promotes a comparable service on its website.Also popular on WSJ.com: We Want to Hear from You
